sources.note: This work describes Yarí [yri] (as a spurious Ethnologue entry; the area's actual languages are named as Carijona [cbd] and Murui Witoto [huu]). The only mention of Yarí in the 205-page file. It is an argument that the Ethnologue entry is spurious (no attested language; the location is Carijona/Murui Witoto territory). No phonological, stress, accent or tone statement about Yarí or any other language appears in the passage. The words 'stress' and 'accent' occur nowhere in the file in a prosodic sense; 'tone/tonal' occurs only in reference-list titles of unrelated works. Cited by the ISO chang…

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2015. Change Request Number 2015-022: retire [yri] Yarí (adopted, effective 2016-01-15). Dallas: SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3(a): 'There is no evidence that the language exists.' Sec. 3(c): Ethnologue listed Yarí as unclassified, 'possibly a dialect of Carijona [cbd] (Carib), a Western Tucanoan language, or Huitoto [huu]'; Wares (1971 letter to B. Grimes) 'existence yet to be confirmed'; name absent from Loukotka 1968, Campbell 1997, Dixon & Aikhenvald 1999, Adelaar & Muysken 2004; Hammarström 2015 concurs, location is Carijona territory; code retired as non-existent.
